entry.evidence: However, the details of this evolution, and the relationship of the Iberian lithosphere to that beneath central Europe remains poorly constrained.

steps.action: The authors pose the question of how the subcontinental mantle beneath central Iberia evolved across two orogenic cycles, and how it relates to the mantle beneath central Europe.
steps.quote: the details of this evolution, and the relationship of the Iberian lithosphere to that beneath central Europe remains poorly constrained

steps.action: They compile 230 whole-rock analyses and 108 Sr-Nd-Pb isotope analyses of ten mafic episodes spanning 575 Ma, mostly taken from the literature (45% of the whole-rock data from their own team).
steps.quote: [...] a trace element and isotope (Sr-Nd-Pb) data set (n = 230) regarding the main ten mafic magmatic episodes

steps.action: They add new measurements to fill gaps: 21 unpublished whole-rock analyses (by ICP-AES/ICP-MS at ACTLABS), 10 new Sr-Nd analyses (by TIMS at UCM) and 10 new Pb analyses (by MC-ICP-MS), with emphasis on the poorly known ALK-1 Almadén rocks.
steps.quote: This contribution includes 21 unpublished analyses

steps.action: They check analytical precision and accuracy against international standards (NIST-694, DNC-1, W-2 and others for trace elements; NBS-987, La Jolla and BHVO-2 for Sr-Nd; NBS 981 and BHVO-2 for Pb).
steps.quote: The BHVO-2 standard was used as a quality control

steps.action: They classify the rocks into calc-alkaline, tholeiitic and alkaline series and ten suites by age, using Nb/Y, TAS and AFM diagrams against reference fields (Fig. 2, Fig. 3, Table 1).
steps.quote: each one subdivided in several suites of different age

steps.action: They restrict interpretation to the most primitive samples (MgO > 4 wt%) and, for altered pre-Variscan rocks such as ALK-1, to elements considered immobile.
steps.quote: the use of incompatible trace element ratios from the most primitive samples (MgO > 4 wt%)

steps.action: They infer source mineralogy (spinel versus garnet lherzolite) and degree of partial melting by fitting REE ratios to non-modal batch-melting curves computed from a single primitive-mantle source.
steps.quote: at the lowest melting fractions of the studied mafic rocks

steps.action: They check the inferred melting depths against the present lithospheric section from geophysics: lithosphere 80-110 km thick and spinel-garnet transition at 50-85 km.
steps.quote: These results are coherent with the Iberian lithospheric section described above.

steps.action: They compare incompatible trace-element ratios (Th/Yb-Ta/Yb, Nb/U-Nb, Zr/Nb-Nb/Th) with MORB, OIB, arc and continental-crust reference fields to characterize the sources.
steps.quote: pointing to derivation from variable enriched mantle sources

steps.action: From the Sr-Nd-Pb isotope arrays they infer at least three mantle components for the alkaline series (PREMA-like, EAR-like, crustal-lithospheric) and two more for the calc-alkaline and tholeiitic series.
steps.quote: indicates the involvement of at least three different mantle components for the alkaline series

steps.action: They match each magmatic episode to a geodynamic setting in published paleogeographic reconstructions (active margin, passive margin, collision, rifting; Fig. 8).
steps.quote: The incoming of intraplate tholeiitic mafic magmas (THOL-1 series) is also coherent with this evolution towards a passive margin scenario

steps.action: For the crustal imprint in the Variscan gabbros they state two rivals: contamination during transport and emplacement, or subduction or delamination of crustal material into the lithospheric mantle.
steps.quote: An alternative possiblity would be the subduction or delamination of the denser granulitic material into the lithospheric mantle

steps.action: They argue against significant emplacement contamination of the primitive appinitic gabbros, citing their own earlier finding that Sr-Nd isotopes do not correlate with SiO2 or LILE.
steps.quote: goes against significant crustal contamination during their emplacement

steps.action: From the time series of initial Sr and Nd ratios compared with felsic fields (Fig. 9), they keep the claim that the deep mantle was metasomatized by subducted continental material after the Variscan collision.
steps.quote: The deep mantle was likely metasomatized by subducted continental material after the Variscan collision

steps.action: They compare the Iberian εNd-time record with the central European record of Dostal et al. (2019b) (Fig. 11).
steps.quote: enable the comparison of their geochemical features with those of the Phanerozoic mafic magmatism

steps.action: They conclude that the pre-Variscan central European mantle was more juvenile and depleted, which places those terranes farther from continental Gondwana than the Central Iberian Zone.
steps.quote: These chemical differences suggest that central Europe terranes would be located farther from continental areas than central Iberia

steps.action: For the long persistence of enriched mantle they state two alternatives: feedback from crustal recycling and delamination during the orogenies, or an old enrichment preserved in the Iberian mantle.
steps.quote: Alternatively, part of this enrichment could be an old feature preserved in the Iberian subcontinental mantle

steps.action: They lean toward the old-enriched-mantle alternative, citing the pre-Variscan isotopes and inherited Proterozoic zircons in the THOL-1 metabasites.
steps.quote: might support this second alternative

steps.action: They compare the magmatic record with the independent mantle-xenolith record (Re-Os model ages, dated metasomatic events) and find only a limited correspondence.
steps.quote: This limits the correlation between outcropping mafic magmatism and the scarce record of old metasomatic events

steps.action: They keep the headline claim of an old enriched subcontinental mantle beneath central Iberia, with post-Variscan asthenospheric rejuvenation.
steps.quote: the existence of an old (pre-Neoproterozoic) enriched subcontinental mantle beneath central Iberia is suggested

end.claim: An old enriched subcontinental lithospheric mantle persisted beneath central Iberia through the Cadomian and Variscan cycles, unlike the more juvenile central European mantle, and was later rejuvenated by post-Variscan asthenospheric upwelling.

decisive_move.sentence: Without assembling the initial Sr-Nd isotope time series of all ten episodes and setting it against the central European record (Fig. 9-11), neither the persistent enriched Iberian mantle nor the contrast with central Europe would be claimed.

gates.evidence: Data were mostly compiled from the literature. New analyses were chosen to fill gaps ('in order to increase the previous scarce geochemical data', p. 5), not to test a stated hypothesis. The headline claim is checked only loosely, through the cited inherited zircons and the xenolith comparison (p. 17). Nothing was fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: Thermal ionization and multicollector ICP mass spectrometry for Sr-Nd-Pb isotope ratios

novelty_claims.quote: To our knowledge, this is the first attempt to get a comprehensive characterization and discussion of the main geochemical, petrogenetic and geodynamic features

limits: The XML text supplied holds only the abstract and the captions, so body steps cite printed pages and quotes come from the PDF text. No review file was supplied, although the acknowledgments mention revision after comments by two referees (J. Mata, S. Aulbach); what changed is not shown. This is a review paper built largely on published data, and the paper does not report how suites, samples and the cut-offs (MgO > 4 wt%, exclusion of the OMZ and GTMZ) were fixed relative to the analysis. The age of the enriched mantle is stated inconsistently: 'pre-Neoproterozoic' (abstract), 'Proterozoic?' (conclusions), 'pre-Phanerozoic' (p. 17). The abstract speaks of 'only minor crustal subduction signatures', while the conclusions speak of 'significant subduction of crustal components'. Sub-claims: classification into ten episodes, best_explanation (descriptive); melt fractions below 2% for ALK-5 and source depths, estimate without stated uncertainty, since a single source composition is assumed (inference: below estimate_with_resolution); paleogeographic position of central Europe relative to Iberia, best_explanation; correlation of xenolith metasomatism with magmatism, no_conclusion. Nd model ages are declared meaningless and used only for comparison. Coding the xenolith comparison as a replication check is a coder judgment: it is weak and did not confirm the claim.

disagreements.target: Early OMZ accretion during the Cadomian orogeny (Ribeiro et al., 2007; Sánchez García et al., 2019)
disagreements.support: Cites differences in Cadomian magmatism, Nd model ages and Ordovician sedimentary features that place the OMZ farther west than the CIZ.
disagreements.quote: Accordingly, we consider that it was during the Variscan collision that these terranes were accreted to form the Iberian Massif.

disagreements.target: Crust-mantle decoupling during the Variscan described for central Europe (Dostal et al., 2019a, 2019b)
disagreements.support: The Iberian εNd record (Fig. 11) shows an enriched lithospheric mantle maintained across the collision and a less abrupt Variscan change.
disagreements.quote: It seems that the described crust-mantle decoupling of central European terranes during the Variscan (Dostal et al., 2019a, 2019b) is not so evident in Iberia

disagreements.target: Late Cambrian-Early Ordovician mantle upwelling and rifting scenario of central Europe (Dostal et al., 2019b) applied to Iberia
disagreements.support: Early Ordovician metabasites are scarce in the CIZ.
disagreements.quote: The scarcity of Early Ordovician metabasites in the Central Iberian Zone does not support a widespread rifting scenario in this microplate at that time

disagreements.target: Asthenospheric affinity of alkaline suites read from trace-element discrimination diagrams
disagreements.support: Only silica-undersaturated rocks with PREMA or EAR isotope features are accepted as asthenosphere-derived, although most alkaline suites plot in the asthenospheric fields.
disagreements.quote: have been documented as derived from the asthenosphere
